title: Implement a Periodic Heartbeat Monitoring Feature
description: Synesthetic Pulse Mesh is a lightweight system monitoring and networking tool written in C. It currently has basic functionality for alerting, security scanning, and load balancing, all driven by a central configuration file and an event bus. The goal of this task is to introduce a new 'heartbeat' feature. This feature will periodically publish an event to the system's event bus, serving as a simple 'I'm alive' signal for external monitoring dashboards. This task will be performed over three distinct development sessions, requiring the agent to retain context between interactions.

project_spec.name: Synesthetic Pulse Mesh
project_spec.description:
Synesthetic Pulse Mesh is an imaginative, small-scale service-mesh simulator written in C where every network packet is represented as a ‘pulse’ of color and sound. The application creates a visual and auditory dashboard that **paints** real-time system events—such as CPU spikes, port scans, and balancing decisions—onto an ANSI-art canvas in the terminal while simultaneously playing short tones via the PC speaker. Each subsystem (monitoring, scanning, alerting, balancing) runs as a lightweight event source; together they form a micro-mesh of services that exchange structured pulses through an in-process event bus. 

Developers can watch the mesh ‘compose’ a live symphony of network health: green pulses sweep left to right when load balancer routes traffic evenly, amber pulses ripple upward on high CPU, and red pulses flash with a warning beep when the security scanner detects suspicious packets. The system purposefully exaggerates events to encourage experimentation—users can inject traffic patterns or trigger synthetic attacks and immediately perceive the outcome through shifting colors and tones. Despite its playful presentation, the project demonstrates core networking concepts such as asynchronous socket IO, service discovery, and command dispatch, all wrapped in an approachable, event-driven architecture ideal for classroom demos or hack-day art installations.
dependencies: pcspkr or SDL2 (optional, for tone generation on *nix)
OpenSSL (TLS handshake stubs for mock secure channels)
uthash (embedded hash maps for service registry)
